headline: Highest risk is data leakage: TREK handles secrets and documents while transformers has broad filesystem and network access, creating a plausible cross-agent exfiltration path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: TREK uses MCP and real-time collaboration, so its outputs can plausibly reach transformers through shared files or tool-mediated handoff; transformers can read files and run browsers, making prompt-like content in documents a realistic injection vector. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred from both profiles and uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF TREK writes attacker-controlled text into a shared file or MCP message that transformers later parses as instructions, injection is possible.
IF an orchestrator copies TREK outputs into transformers prompts without sanitization, the pathway activates.
mitigations: Disable automatic handoff of TREK outputs into transformers prompts.
Add a strict delimiter/template around any transferred text.
Strip instructions from documents before passing them onward.
Review shared files for prompt-like content before ingestion.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and instruction/content separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK explicitly touches API keys, MFA secrets, confirmation numbers, and documents, while transformers has broad filesystem read/write and broad network egress. If they share a workspace or files, transformers can read sensitive TREK data and potentially transmit it outward. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default self-hosted setups, so severity is high.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same directory or mounted volume, TREK secrets can be read by transformers.
IF transformers forwards file contents to remote inference or APIs, sensitive TREK data can leave the environment.
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different volumes.
Remove secrets from any shared workspace.
Restrict transformers to a read-only, redacted input set.
Block outbound network for any process handling TREK secrets.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage and egress policy isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write files and both support multiple instances; TREK is collaborative and transformers can spawn subprocesses and write the filesystem. Without documented locking or isolation, concurrent writes to shared files or state can collide. The overlap is real but not inherently irreversible, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace or database path, file clobbering can occur.
IF TREK and transformers are run concurrently without locks, state races become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Use file locks around shared artifacts.
Make one agent read-only on shared paths.
Serialize writes during collaborative sessions.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in, and transformers produces document-processing outputs that may be treated as authoritative by downstream tooling. If TREK consumes transformers output without verification, errors can cascade into plans, reservations, or user-facing documents. The pathway exists, but no direct action-taking chain is documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF TREK ingests transformers-generated text as trusted facts, downstream planning errors can propagate.
IF transformers outputs are used to populate reservations or travel documents without review, the cascade activates.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on generated facts.
Cross-check outputs against source documents.
Mark AI-generated fields as untrusted by default.
Log provenance for any copied facts.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before reservations or commits.

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles country visit history, user accounts, email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets, while transformers touches multimodal documents and files. If TREK data is routed into transformers without residency or retention controls, compliance gaps can arise. The profiles do not specify a direct residency mismatch, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF TREK data containing personal or secret material is stored in a transformers-accessible workspace, retention and access controls may diverge.
IF logs or uploads preserve travel records longer than intended, subject-rights handling can fail.
mitigations: Minimize personal data copied between agents.
Set short retention on shared logs and uploads.
Redact secrets before transfer.
Document which agent stores which data class.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies across both systems.
